finding.text: `week.json` — the source for all 5 stat cards — is still a hand-run snapshot, not live, so the owner's core ask ("shouldn't this be computed in real time by node... this shouldn't be stale data") is unmet. `Server/week-cost.mjs`'s own header still reads "Run by hand to (re)write... node Server/week-cost.mjs"; `readme.md` says "Re-run it to refresh them." doc/decisions.md explains a live route/watcher needs files outside the fence, but the brief's own named fallback (a small standalone script that re-runs the computation on an interval when started, documented as a decision) wasn't tried either — only the reconciliation bug was fixed, not the staleness itself.

The grid's own Role column still prints raw role strings ("cli", "vscode mastermind") instead of the plain labels used in the filter row and the "by role" list — contradicts the scope-narrowed ask: "give the role-filter checkboxes **and any place these words show** plain names." Evidence: `shots/.../1200.png`, Role column — "cli" and "vscode / mastermind" (two lines) are shown verbatim; `row_view()` in `page.js` is unchanged in the diff, only the filter checkboxes and the "by role" list call `role_label()`.

The "Per 1% of your weekly plan" card reads as a bare em dash "—" (current data: $0 Claude this week) with no `title=` explaining why, unlike the other cards. Evidence: `shots/.../1920.png` and `3440.png`, 4th stat tile.

answer.reply: fixed: Server/week-cost.mjs now exports write_week() and gains --watch [minutes] (default 10), a plain standalone loop that re-runs the same real compute_window() on an interval and rewrites week.json -- the brief's own named fallback, no HTTP route or dev-server watcher needed. week.json's own note field says which mode wrote it.
fixed: row_view()'s Role cell now calls role_label() too, same as the filter row and the "by role" list, with the matching title= tooltip.

fixed: the "Per 1% of your weekly plan" tile's blank state now gets its own title= explaining why it's blank (no real Claude $ or percent-used yet to divide), instead of reusing the has-a-number tooltip.
